title: Crete
lead: Crete is the large island south of the Aegean Sea. The Old Testament may name it as Caphtor, the homeland of the Philistines (Amos 9:7; Jeremiah 47:4); in the New Testament Cretans hear the apostles at Pentecost (Acts 2:11), Paul's prison ship shelters along its coast (Acts 27:7-21), and Paul leaves Titus there to lead its churches (Titus 1:5).

sections.b: Amos says the LORD brought "the Philistines from Caphtor" (Amos 9:7), and Jeremiah calls the Philistines "the remnant of the island of Caphtor" (Jeremiah 47:4). Some identify Caphtor with Crete; others look elsewhere in the eastern Mediterranean. The Bible does not name Crete in the Old Testament, so the link rests on the identification of Caphtor.

Cretans were among the Jews and converts in Jerusalem at Pentecost: "Some are Cretans and Arabs" (Acts 2:11). Paul's ship to Rome crept "along the sheltered side of Crete" (Acts 27:7), put in at Fair Havens near Lasea, and was driven off by a storm when it tried to reach Phoenix (Acts 27:8-21). The letter to Titus assumes churches in many of the island's towns (Titus 1:5) and quotes a Cretan poet on the islanders' bad name (Titus 1:12).
